newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money falls to 5.5/6.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money falls to 5.5/6.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged down to 5.5/6.0 percent on Monday from around 6.5/7.0 percent at the opening on sustained ample supply, dealers said.
Dealers said carry-forward liquidity and central bank supply of 834 billion rupiah continued to keep the market flush.

Some 895 billion rupiah of central bank certificates (SBIs) were due today, compared with some 11 billion rupiah of maturing short-term papers (SBPUs) and some 50 billion rupiah of SBIs to be settled today.
Dealers said sentiment on the rupiah stayed weak as the flush market kept the returns on rupiah less attractive.
One- and three-month money were at 10.75/11.00 and 12.75/13.00 percent, respectively.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates stable. It offered seven-day SBIs at 6.5 percent, 14-day at 8.5 percent and one-month at 10.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 8.74 percent against 5.83 percent on Thursday.
